rules.intensity: Tight or mildly uncomfortable, never painful (about 5-7/10)
rules.weeklyTargetLabel: Delphi 'highest sustainable volume' (above the ~10 min/week plateau; Konrad caveat for high flexibility goals)
rules.loadRule: RPE-based: rating <=3 +1 kg (or harder tempo), 4 +0.5 kg, 5-7 hold, >=8 or pain -1 kg

sources.cite: Konrad, Warneke et al. 2023, J Sport Health Sci: chronic stretching meta-analysis
sources.used: Static and PNF beat dynamic for chronic ROM; volume, intensity, frequency and age not significant moderators; women gained more than men (p=0.04); null dose results may not hold for extreme flexibility goals

sources.cite: Delphi consensus of stretching experts 2025, J Sport Health Sci
sources.used: 2-3 sets daily, 30-120 s per muscle, highest sustainable weekly volume; static <=60 s per muscle before performance (inside a dynamic warm-up is fine); no overall injury-risk reduction; largely ineffective for post-exercise recovery; chronic stiffness loss may affect stretch-shortening performance

sources.cite: Ingram et al. 2025, Sports Med: static stretching dose meta-regression (189 studies)
sources.used: Gains plateau ~4 min/session (acute) and ~10 min/week cumulative per muscle (chronic); intensity, age, frequency don't moderate; poor baseline gains more

sources.cite: Afonso et al. 2021, strength training vs stretching
sources.used: Strength training equals stretching for ROM

sources.cite: Alizadeh et al. 2023, Sports Med: resistance training and ROM
sources.used: Loaded RT improves ROM; bodyweight-only not significant -> prefer external load; trained/active people gain less (ES 0.43 vs 1.04)

sources.cite: Warneke et al. 2024, Sports Med Open: stretching, strength and hypertrophy
sources.used: Small strength side-benefit with longer durations

sources.cite: Nakamura et al. 2024, Frontiers in Medicine: static stretching in older adults (73.8 y)
sources.used: 4x30 s calf stretching, >=3x/week, 10 weeks: +9 deg dorsiflexion (d=1.37); tissue hardness also fell (d=-0.27) but did not correlate with the ROM gain

sources.cite: Mariani et al. 2024, Sport Sci Health: static stretching and stiffness in older adults
sources.used: Chronic stretching reduces stiffness in older adults

sources.cite: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription (11th ed., 2021): flexibility FITT
sources.used: 10-30 s holds for most adults, 30-60 s for older adults; >=2-3 days/week, ideally daily; ~60 s total per joint; to tightness or slight discomfort

sources.cite: Behm et al. 2023, acute stretching meta-analysis
sources.used: ACUTE only: single bout gives small ROM gain; adductor test not significant (not used for chronic rules)

sources.cite: Behm, Aragão-Santos, Korooshfard, Anvar 2023, IJSPT: Alternative Flexibility Training (commentary)
sources.used: Commentary: RT/foam rolling also raise ROM; stretching adds more when ROM is the goal. Its injury claim conflicts with the Delphi (no overall injury reduction), so the app makes NO injury-prevention claims

sources.cite: Thomas et al. 2018, Int J Sports Med: stretch dose and frequency systematic review
sources.used: >=5 min/week per muscle needed; 5-10 vs >10 min/week NS; per-session duration NS; >=5 days/week better than 2-3

sources.cite: Weppler & Magnusson 2010, Phys Ther: increasing muscle extensibility (sensory theory)
sources.used: Gains largely from stretch tolerance; partly reversible when stopping -> maintenance mode; no promise of tissue lengthening

changelog.change: Peer review folded in (SCIENCE-REVIEW.md): hold cap 60 s default, frequency >=5 d/wk, weekly-time progression, RPE loads, looser overlap rule (0.7), pattern >=3x/wk, no injury/recovery claims, source fixes
